column5: Description
Repositories, Harness CI/CD, OpenShift preprod deployment, connectivity to Azure and the internal LLM, logging and alerting for Loss Run Intake.
Microsoft Entra ID sign-in, token validation, user provisioning, roles and per-agent permissions.
Azure SQL data model and migrations, ADLS Gen2 file storage, UAT data preparation.
FastAPI endpoints, background extraction worker, reconciliation engine and golden-source Excel export.
Port the existing LLM extraction code behind the LLMIntake interface (recommend_page, infer_fields, extract_claims), internal LLM client, large-document handling and accuracy evaluation.
React frontend built from the Figma designs: app shell, dashboard, upload, job detail, agent builder wizard, team management.
Dependency and image scanning, audit logging and data retention for real loss run data used in UAT.
UAT planning, user provisioning, UI acceptance, documentation, UAT execution and go/no-go recommendation.

column4: [1.1] Set up backend and frontend repositories
column5:
h3. Context
Two repositories, one image each: loss-run-intake-backend (Python FastAPI API and worker, same image) and loss-run-intake-frontend (React SPA plus a small Node server that serves it and proxies /api).

h3. Scope
* Create both repositories in GHE with main as default branch
* Branch protection on main: PR required, at least 1 review, CI must pass
* PR template, CODEOWNERS and README with local development setup
* .env.example in each repository; no secrets committed

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Both repositories exist with protected main
* A new developer can run backend and frontend locally by following the README

column4: [1.2] Verify connectivity from preprod to Azure SQL, ADLS, Entra ID and internal LLM
column5:
h3. Context
Azure SQL, the ADLS Gen2 container and the service principal already exist. Network egress from the OpenShift preprod namespace (0328axio-01-preprod-axa-xl) has not been verified.

h3. Scope
* Store service principal credentials, SQL connection details and LLM API key in an OpenShift Secret (never in the repository)
* From a debug pod in the preprod namespace, test Azure SQL (port 1433), the ADLS endpoint (443), login.microsoftonline.com (443) and the internal LLM endpoint
* Raise firewall / egress requests for anything that is blocked

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Every endpoint is reachable from a pod in preprod; results recorded in this ticket
* Service principal can connect to Azure SQL and read/write a test file in the ADLS container

h3. Notes
* Start on day 1: egress requests can take time and block 1.8, 1.9 and 1.12

column4: [1.3] Harness CI build pipelines for backend and frontend images
column5:
h3. Context
Harness project xlcapp0328axio; images are pushed to Artifactory with the xlc-panda-buildah plugin.

h3. Scope
* Backend: Run step installs Python dependencies into pydeps, runs pytest, then buildah builds and pushes
* Frontend: Run step runs npm ci and npm run build, then buildah builds and pushes
* Image tag <+pipeline.sequenceId>

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* A merge to main produces both images in Artifactory
* Failing unit tests or build errors fail the pipeline

h3. Notes
* Dockerfiles must not contain RUN instructions: the buildah plugin runs unprivileged without network, so all installs/builds happen in Run steps
* The Run step image must match the Dockerfile base image (compiled wheels)
* Check that the repo field is the real Artifactory path, not a placeholder

column4: [1.4] Harness CD deployment to OpenShift preprod
column5:
h3. Context
Deploy api, worker and frontend to preprod. With files in ADLS and data in Azure SQL, no PVC is needed and api/worker run as separate Deployments.

h3. Scope
* Manifests: Deployments for api, worker and frontend; Services; Route (router: internal) to the frontend; ConfigMap; Secret reference
* api probes: startupProbe and livenessProbe on /healthz, readinessProbe on /readyz, explicit timeoutSeconds
* worker probes: startupProbe and livenessProbe checking the heartbeat file age, explicit timeoutSeconds
* Resource requests and limits for every container
* Harness deploy stage with values file image: <+artifacts.primary.image>

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* All pods Running and Ready with zero restarts over 1 hour
* Route URL loads the frontend and /api calls are proxied to the backend
* Total CPU/memory limits fit the namespace quota; a quota increase request is raised if they do not (only about 0.7 CPU was free at last check)

h3. Notes
* Route to.name must match the actual Service name
* Every manifest file (ConfigMap, Service, Route) must be listed in the Harness manifest paths

h3. Context
Single app registration used by the SPA to sign in and by the backend to validate tokens.

h3. Scope
* SPA platform with redirect URI = preprod Route URL (plus http://localhost:5173 for local development)
* Expose an API with scope api://<client-id>/access_as_user
* App role LossRun.Admin

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Tenant ID and client ID documented and stored in the ConfigMap
* A test user can obtain a token containing the access_as_user scope

h3. Notes
* May require a request to the identity team

column4: [1.6] Backend Entra token validation and user provisioning
column5:
h3. Context
The backend accepts only valid Entra access tokens and maps them to application users.

h3. Scope
* Validate signature (cached JWKS), issuer, audience, expiry, tenant and access_as_user scope
* Match users by Entra oid; create the user on first login; link pre-invited members by email
* Read app roles from the token
* Public /api/config endpoint returns auth mode and SPA client settings
* AUTH_MODE=dev for local development

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Missing, invalid or expired token returns 401
* A valid token creates or links the user record
* Unit tests use locally signed tokens (no calls to Entra in CI)

h3. Context
The SPA signs users in with their corporate account using MSAL redirect flow.

h3. Scope
* Load /api/config before rendering, then initialise MSAL
* Attach bearer token to every API call; silent token renewal; sign-out
* If /api/config fails, show an error page with Retry instead of a blank page

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* User signs in with a corporate account, sees their name in the header and can sign out
* Token expiry is handled without a manual page reload

column4: [1.8] Data model and Azure SQL schema migrations with Alembic
column5:
h3. Context
Persistent model for users, teams, agents (extraction schemas), jobs, documents, extracted claims and issues.

h3. Scope
* SQLAlchemy models and Alembic migrations; mssql-python driver with Encrypt=yes
* SQL Server-safe types: String(36) UUIDs, NVARCHAR(max) for JSON, no multiple cascade paths
* Migrations run as an explicit step (Harness step or Kubernetes Job) before rollout, not on app startup

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* alembic upgrade head runs cleanly against preprod Azure SQL
* Downgrade of the latest migration is tested

column4: [1.9] ADLS Gen2 storage adapter for uploads and exports
column5:
h3. Context
Uploaded loss run files and generated exports are stored in the existing ADLS Gen2 container.

h3. Scope
* Storage interface with ADLS implementation (service principal) and local filesystem implementation for development
* Path convention per environment / team / job for originals and exports
* Stream uploads and downloads instead of buffering whole files in memory

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Uploads and exports land in ADLS; no PVC is used
* Integration test passes against the preprod container

h3. Context
Endpoints the frontend uses to submit files and track extraction jobs.

h3. Scope
* Upload endpoint for PDF, XLSX, XLS and CSV with configurable size limit
* Create job (file + agent), list jobs (paged, filtered), job detail
* Job statuses: queued, running, succeeded, failed

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Unsupported type or oversize file returns 4xx with a clear message
* Users only see jobs they are allowed to access
* OpenAPI documentation available

h3. Context
A separate Deployment using the backend image with command python -m lossrun.worker.

h3. Scope
* Poll queued jobs and claim them atomically
* Status transitions, error capture, requeue of stale jobs
* Write a heartbeat file for the liveness probe
* Handle SIGTERM gracefully: finish the current file within the termination grace period

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Two worker replicas never process the same job (tested)
* A job held by a killed worker is requeued after the timeout
* Failed jobs store an error message shown in the UI

column4: [1.12] Port existing LLM extraction code: extract_claims
column5:
h3. Context
LLM extraction logic already exists outside this repository. Move it behind the LLMIntake interface (recommend_page, infer_fields, extract_claims).

h3. Scope
* Review the existing code's inputs and outputs and map them to the interface
* Implement extract_claims: document pages + agent field schema -> claim rows
* Validate and normalise output to field types (dates, amounts, currency)
* Unit tests with recorded LLM responses (no live LLM calls in CI)
* Prompts versioned in the repository

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Worker extracts claims end to end from a sample PDF and a sample Excel loss run in preprod
* Malformed LLM output fails the job with a readable error instead of crashing the worker

h3. Context
Client used by all LLMIntake methods to call the internal LLM service.

h3. Scope
* Endpoint, model and API key from environment / Secret
* Timeout and retry with backoff for 429 and 5xx; classify retryable vs non-retryable errors
* Log latency and token usage without logging document content
* LLM_PROVIDER switch to select provider

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Configuration is environment-only; nothing hard-coded
* Retry behaviour verified with a mocked endpoint

h3. Context
Base frontend project matching the Figma design system.

h3. Scope
* Vite + React + TypeScript + TanStack Router/Query + Tailwind
* Design tokens (colours, typography, spacing) taken from Figma
* App shell: header, navigation, page layout
* Base components: button, input, table, badge, dialog, toast
* Node server serves the built SPA and proxies /api to the backend Service (streaming, long timeout for uploads)

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Shell matches the Figma layout
* Lint and type check run in CI
* Image runs in preprod behind the Route

h3. Context
Users see their jobs and submit new loss run files.

h3. Scope
* Dashboard: job list with status badges, auto-refresh while jobs are running
* Upload page: drag and drop, file type and size validation, agent selection, upload progress

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Pages match Figma
* A successful upload creates a job and navigates to its detail page

column4: [1.16] Job detail page with extracted claims and Excel download
column5:
h3. Context
Users review the extraction result of a job.

h3. Scope
* Job status and metadata
* Extracted claims table with sorting and horizontal scroll
* Download Excel button
* Polling while the job is running

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Page matches Figma
* Download returns the golden-source Excel for the job

h3. Context
Standard Excel output that downstream teams consume.

h3. Scope
* Generate XLSX in the golden-source layout from a job's claims
* Store the file in ADLS; download endpoint with access check

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Column order and formats follow the agreed template (confirm with business)
* Dates and amounts are typed cells; file opens in Excel without warnings

h3. Context
An agent defines which fields to extract (name, type, description, required) for a carrier or format.

h3. Scope
* Create, read, update, delete and clone agents
* Golden agent: organisation default, editable by Admin only
* Editing an agent does not change results of completed jobs

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* All endpoints enforce permissions
* Deleting an agent that is in use is blocked or soft-deleted

h3. Context
LLM methods used by the agent builder wizard, moved from the existing code behind LLMIntake.

h3. Scope
* recommend_page: from a sample document, return the page(s) most likely to contain the claims table, with confidence
* infer_fields: propose a field list with types from the selected page
* Reuse the LLM client from 1.13

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Both methods return usable results on the evaluation samples
* Low-confidence results are flagged instead of silently guessed

h3. Context
Three-step wizard for building a new agent from a sample loss run.

h3. Scope
* Step 1: upload a sample file
* Step 2: preview pages, highlight the recommended page, user selects
* Step 3: review inferred fields (rename, change type, mark required, add, remove) and save

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Wizard matches Figma
* A user can complete the wizard end to end and use the new agent on a job
* Going back to a previous step keeps entered data

column4: [2.4] Reconciliation rules engine and issues API
column5:
h3. Context
Automatic data quality checks on extracted claims.

h3. Scope
* Rules: missing required fields, invalid dates, paid + reserve vs incurred mismatch, negative amounts, duplicate claim numbers, totals vs document totals where available
* Issues stored with severity, row and field
* Endpoints to list, resolve and ignore issues

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Every rule has unit tests
* Resolved values are reflected in the Excel export

column4: [2.5] Job detail enhancements: preview, issues, inline edit, re-run
column5:
h3. Context
Users verify and correct extraction results against the source document.

h3. Scope
* Document preview: PDF page render; spreadsheet preview served by the backend
* Issues panel; clicking an issue highlights the row/cell
* Inline edit of cell values (audited)
* Re-run the job with the same or a different agent

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Page matches Figma
* Edits are reflected in the export
* Re-run creates a new job and keeps history

h3. Context
Clean spreadsheet loss runs can be mapped by column headers without calling the LLM, saving cost and time.

h3. Scope
* Header row detection
* Synonym-based mapping of columns to agent fields
* Fall back to the LLM when mapping confidence is low

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Clean Excel/CSV samples are extracted without LLM calls
* Mapping decisions are logged

h3. Context
Loss runs can run to hundreds of pages.

h3. Scope
* Configurable limits on pages and file size
* Chunk pages for extract_claims; merge results and de-duplicate across chunk boundaries
* Token budget per job with a clear error when exceeded

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* A 100+ page PDF completes without timeout or OOM within worker limits
* Limits are shown to users in the UI

column4: [2.8] Extraction evaluation set and accuracy report
column5:
h3. Context
Objective measure of extraction quality, used as a UAT entry criterion.

h3. Scope
* Collect sample loss runs from at least 10 carriers with hand-labelled expected output
* Script computing field-level precision and recall
* Run on demand (not in CI with live LLM)

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Baseline accuracy report published
* Report agreed with business as UAT entry criterion

h3. Context
Control who can manage the team and which agents each user can use.

h3. Scope
* Admin vs User from the Entra app role
* Admin manages team members and per-agent access
* Enforced in the backend, not only hidden in the UI

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Authorization tests cover every endpoint
* Users only see jobs and agents they are allowed to access

h3. Context
Admin page for managing users and access.

h3. Scope
* Invite members by email
* Set role
* Grant or revoke agent access

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Page matches Figma
* Visible to Admins only

column4: [2.11] Empty, error and loading states per Figma
column5:
h3. Context
Consistent handling of non-happy-path states across all pages.

h3. Scope
* Empty states for lists
* Error states for failed requests and failed jobs, with retry where useful
* Loading skeletons

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Every page has empty, error and loading states matching Figma

h3. Context
Troubleshooting a job across frontend proxy, api and worker.

h3. Scope
* JSON logs in api and worker
* Request ID passed from the frontend proxy to the api, stored on the job and used in worker logs
* No personal data or document content in logs

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* A job can be traced in OpenShift logs by its job ID

h3. Context
Define how UAT is run in preprod and what counts as passing.

h3. Scope
* Test scenarios and test cases
* Carriers and sample files covered
* Acceptance criteria (including the accuracy baseline from 2.8)
* Participating business users and schedule

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Plan reviewed and approved by the business owner

h3. Context
UAT participants need access to preprod.

h3. Scope
* Assign UAT users / group in Entra, including LossRun.Admin where needed
* Pre-create team members in the application

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Every UAT participant can sign in and sees the correct role

column4: [3.3] UAT data preparation and golden agents
column5:
h3. Context
UAT uses real loss runs, which contain claimant data.

h3. Scope
* Obtain data-policy approval for using real samples in preprod, or mask them
* Pre-configure golden agents for the carriers in scope

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Approved sample set available to UAT users
* Golden agents produce expected results on the sample set

h3. Context
Security baseline before real data is used in UAT.

h3. Scope
* Dependency scan for backend and frontend
* Container image scan per AXA XL standard
* Fix critical and high findings

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* No open critical or high findings, or documented exceptions approved

h3. Context
Accountability and retention for real loss run data.

h3. Scope
* Audit log of upload, download, edit, delete and role changes (who and when)
* Retention policy for files and extracted data in preprod (confirm period with data governance)
* Automated clean-up job

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Audit entries visible to Admins
* Data older than the retention period is removed automatically

h3. Context
Confirm preprod can handle UAT load within the namespace quota.

h3. Scope
* Concurrent jobs from several users
* Large PDFs
* Tune worker replicas and resources within quota

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Results documented with expected processing times
* No OOM kills or quota errors during the test

h3. Context
Know about problems during UAT before users report them.

h3. Scope
* Alerts on job failure rate, LLM errors and pod restarts using the platform's monitoring stack

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Alerts reach the team channel or email
* Each alert tested once

column4: [3.8] UI acceptance against Figma and browser compatibility
column5:
h3. Context
Final visual and functional check before UAT users start.

h3. Scope
* Page-by-page comparison with Figma
* Check supported browsers (Edge, Chrome)
* Basic accessibility checks (keyboard navigation, contrast)

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* All deviations fixed or accepted by design

column4: [3.9] User guide and UAT feedback channel
column5:
h3. Context
UAT users need instructions and a way to report issues.

h3. Scope
* Short user guide (upload, review, fix issues, export, build an agent)
* Feedback channel: Jira issue type or form for UAT defects

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Guide shared with UAT users
* Defects reported during UAT land in Jira

column4: [3.10] UAT execution and bug fix buffer
column5:
h3. Context
Run UAT with business users and fix defects found.

h3. Scope
* Support UAT sessions
* Triage and fix defects
* Redeploy fixes to preprod

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* All planned test cases executed
* No open critical or high defects at the end of UAT

column4: [3.11] UAT sign-off summary and go/no-go recommendation
column5:
h3. Context
Close UAT with a clear decision on moving to production.

h3. Scope
* Summary of test results, accuracy, open defects and risks
* Go/no-go recommendation for production

h3. Acceptance Criteria
* Summary reviewed with business owner and decision recorded
